name: Budgie
description: Desktop environment by Buddies of Budgie.
summary: AI/LLM-generated code is forbidden in Budgie 11 codebases, including budgie-desktop-services, and AI research is not encouraged there. In the listed Budgie 10 projects, documentation center and website, generated code is conditionally allowed with testing, Assisted-by attribution and meaningful human control, but end-to-end agents are rejected; AI-assisted written content needs no Assisted-by trailer, though wholly generated content without meaningful human involvement is unacceptable.

evidence.quote: Buddies of Budgie follows a human-centric development model. It is our position that only humans can be authors and ultimately be held accountable.
A high-level summary of our policy section for this category: Use of AI / LLMs for code generation is permitted, so long as it:
Non-trivial AI-assisted code must be built, installed, and tested by the contributor
When AI tools assisted with code changes (writing, modifying, or generating code), add an Assisted-by trailer to the commit message with the tool and model identifier.
You must have an understanding of the proposed fix, collaborate on architectural decisions (or make them fully yourself), and not simply leave critical decisions up to the model
All contributions must be tested before submission.
AI performed purely mechanical tasks like formatting, running commands, or committing (e.g. using any commit skill we may have)
AI was used for research only - asking questions, understanding APIs, exploring approaches - but the human wrote all the code
A high-level summary of our policy section for this category: Use of AI / LLMs for code generation is forbidden and will be wholesale rejected.
Involves a human in the loop and is audited. Simply saying "keep me in the loop" does not count.

In this specific category, contributors are generally free to make their own informed choices about which tools they use; however, end-to-end agentic workflows are soundly rejected, as they would violate our human-centric development model and "human-in-the-loop" requirement.
The attribution requirements in this policy are specific to source code contributions. Blog posts and other written content are a different matter.
AI tools may be used to assist with writing blog posts, release announcements, and other project communications. No Assisted-by attribution is required for written content.
The author is still expected to review, refine, and stand behind what is published; the final voice should be theirs.
Content that is wholly generated by AI tooling without meaningful human involvement is never acceptable.
Readers should never expect that a blog post or any form of written content by Buddies of Budgie was produced entirely by AI.
There is always a human involved in the process of shaping the narrative, ensuring accuracy, and making it their own.

They can help explore ideas, work with the author to draft or explore technical implementations, accelerate development, and improve the clarity of how we communicate, whether in blog posts, issues, or the changes described in pull requests.
AI was used to help write documentation for issues or pull requests (not committed code)

The author is still expected to review, refine, and stand behind what is published; the final voice should be theirs.
Content that is wholly generated by AI tooling without meaningful human involvement is never acceptable.
Readers should never expect that a blog post or any form of written content by Buddies of Budgie was produced entirely by AI.
There is always a human involved in the process of shaping the narrative, ensuring accuracy, and making it their own.
Ensure all relevant commits include the Assisted-by trailer and align with our Contributing documentation
Ensure an Assisted-by trailer is included at the end of any summary section of the work (before any section for tests / test plan)
Your test plan should reflect that you actually built, installed, and verified the changes
Supplemental comments on the PR with AI prompt/planning information are welcome and encouraged for research and learnings, but not mandatory
However, AI planning documents should not be committed to the source repository. Share them as PR comments instead.
Intentional obfuscation of AI tooling usage is grounds for rejection and may result in being blocked from future contributions.

On the first violation you will be provided a warning unless the violation is deemed severe enough by a member of "Best Buds" (for example, en masse PR submissions or clearly fully agentic submissions)
After one warning, any future violations will result in you being blocked from future contributions
When a violation occurs, your contribution can be rejected, reverted, or rewritten

Therefore, it is the policy of the Buddies of Budgie team that no components associated with Budgie 11 (including budgie-desktop-services, which is used for both Budgie 10.10.x and Budgie 11) shall include any code generated by "AI" / large-language models.
No codebase within this category has included code generated by an AI / LLM as of the updating of this policy on October 17th, 2026, and none will going forward.
Any use of AI / LLMs for alternative use cases, such as for research purposes, is not endorsed by the project.
While we cannot control how one uses these tools beyond code generation, we will not encourage using them for research purposes either.
